args.content:
# srgn — TypeScript & C prepared query scopes: behavioral specification

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (invoked as `/workspace/executable`; clap usage/error
lines print the argv0-derived name `executable`, except one custom error that hardcodes
`srgn` — noted below). All findings obtained by black-box observation only.

NOTE ON FILE NAME: the task-requested file name exceeded the 255-byte filesystem limit;
this shortened name is used instead.

---

## 1. Search-mode output format (language scopes, no actions)

Giving a language scope (`--typescript <value>`, `--c <value>`, `--*-query`,
`--*-query-file`) without any action puts srgn in **search mode**. Output on stdout,
one line per input line that contains at least one in-scope byte range:

```
<stdin-or-filename>:<line>:<start>-<end>[;<start>-<end>...]:<full original line content>
```

- `(stdin)` is the literal prefix when reading stdin; a real path (`files/one.ts`) when
  working on files via `-G`.
- `<line>` is 1-based.
- `<start>`/`<end>` are **0-based BYTE offsets within that line, start-inclusive,
  end-exclusive** (verified with multibyte input: `"héllo 😀"` string content gives
  `11-22` — bytes, not chars).
- Multiple disjoint ranges on one line are `;`-separated, ascending. Overlapping ranges
  (e.g. produced by `-j` joins of nested scopes) are **merged** into one range.
- The full original line text (including any `\r` of CRLF input) is printed after the
  last `:`.
- Lines are only printed if they contain ≥1 scoped byte. A multi-line scoped node prints
  every line it touches: first line `<startcol>-<linelen>`, middle lines `0-<linelen>`,
  last line `0-<endcol>`.
- Output preserves the input's final-newline state (no trailing newline added/removed).
- `--only-matching` produces byte-identical output in this mode (no observable effect).
- `--line-numbers` has no observable effect in search mode (already numbered).
- There is **no `--count` flag** in this build despite the README
  (`error: unexpected argument '--count' found` + tip `a similar argument exists: '--c'`, exit 2).

### TTY vs pipe

- Piped (or `--stdout-detection force-pipe`): format as above, no ANSI color codes ever.
- TTY (or `--stdout-detection force-tty`): **no byte ranges are shown**. stdin input
  prints `<line>:<content>`. File input prints a header line with the file name, then
  `<line>:<content>` lines, then a blank line; files separated by blank lines:
  ```
  files/one.ts
  1:const a = "x";

  files/two.ts
  1:const b = "y";
  ```
- No ANSI colors were emitted in either mode (checked with `script -qec ... | od -c`),
  including error messages.

### Action-mode note

With an action (replacement, `-d`, `--upper`, ...), stdout is the full transformed
document. With `--line-numbers` added in action mode, output switches to the annotated
form `(stdin):<line>:<ranges>:<modified-line-content>` showing only lines with matches.

---

## 2. Exit codes and error messages (verbatim)

| Condition | stdout | stderr | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search mode, zero in-scope bytes (incl. empty input) | empty | `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` | 1 |
| Action mode, zero in-scope bytes | input unchanged | empty | 0 |
| `--fail-any` and something matched | (normal) | `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope` | 1 |
| `--fail-none` and nothing matched | (normal) | `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` | 1 |
| `--fail-any`/`--fail-none` satisfied | normal | empty | 0 |
| Invalid prepared value (`--typescript bogus`) | empty | clap error (below) | 2 |
| `--typescript` + `--typescript-query` together | empty | clap conflict error (below) | 2 |
| `--c` + `--typescript` (two languages) | empty | `error: Can only use one language at a time.` | 2 |
| Invalid custom query syntax/node/field | empty | `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: ...` | 1 |
| Missing `--*-query-file` | empty | `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` | 1 |
| Invalid UTF-8 on stdin | empty | `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8` | 1 |
| No actions and no language scope (not search mode) | input unchanged | `[<RFC3339 timestamp> ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.` | 0 |

Verbatim clap errors (stderr; `executable` is argv0 here):

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--typescript <TYPESCRIPT>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, function, async-function, sync-function, method, constructor, class, enum, interface, try-catch, var-decl, let, const, var, type-params, type-alias, namespace, export]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--c <C>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, includes, type-def, enum, struct, variable, function, function-def, function-decl, switch, if, for, while, do, union, identifier, declaration, call-expression]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
Values are case-sensitive; a near-miss appends a tip line between the possible-values
line and the blank line:
```
  tip: a similar value exists: 'comments'
```
The `~PATTERN` dynamic syntax exists only for some Go/Rust values; for TS/C e.g.
`--typescript 'class~K'` is an invalid value (with tip `a similar value exists: 'class'`).

Conflict error:
```
error: the argument '--typescript <TYPESCRIPT>' cannot be used with '--typescript-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --typescript <TYPESCRIPT> [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
(analogous for `--c` / `--c-query`).

Two-languages error — note the usage line here hardcodes `srgn`, not argv0:
```
error: Can only use one language at a time.

Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Custom query compile errors (all `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at <row>:<col>. ...`, exit 1):
- `--typescript-query '(('`:
  ```
  Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:3. Invalid syntax:
  ((
    ^
  ```
  (the query text and a caret pointing at the offending column are echoed)
- `--typescript-query 'identifier'` (bare word, invalid syntax):
  ```
  Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:1. Invalid syntax:
  identifier
  ^
  ```
- `--typescript-query '(bogus_node)'`:
  `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type bogus_node`
- `--c-query '(declaration bogus: (identifier))'`:
  `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:14. Invalid field name bogus`
- A syntactically valid query with **no `@capture`** (e.g. `(identifier)`) compiles but
  scopes nothing → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit 1 in search mode.
- Custom query scopes = **every captured node, exactly as captured** (quotes NOT stripped;
  e.g. `(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @name value: (string) @val)` on
  `const STR = "double";` yields ranges `6-9;12-20` — `STR` and `"double"` with quotes).
- Prepared-value flag and custom query for the SAME language are mutually exclusive
  (clap error above), but prepared values of one language may be repeated freely.

---

## 3. Scope combination semantics (AND / `-j` OR)

- Repeating a language flag (`--typescript class --typescript method`) **intersects**
  scopes, left to right. Intersection is sequential narrowing: the next query is
  evaluated **only within the regions left in scope by the previous one** (behaviorally:
  everything outside the current scope is masked out, offsets preserved, and the next
  query's captures are found in what remains). Consequences:
  - `--typescript const --typescript var-decl` on `const s = "a";` → `6-13` (declarator
    inside declaration). OK.
  - `--typescript var-decl --typescript const` → nothing (`No input was in scope`):
    no `const` declaration survives inside a bare declarator region.
  - `--typescript class --typescript method` → methods. `--typescript method --typescript class` → nothing.
  - `--typescript strings --typescript strings` → **nothing** (TS string scopes exclude
    quotes/escapes, so the leftover fragments no longer parse as strings). But
    `--c strings --c strings` **works** (C string scopes include the quotes, so the
    masked text still parses as a string literal).
  - `--typescript comments --typescript comments` and `--typescript class --typescript class` work.
- `-j`/`--join-language-scopes` unions all language scopes (order irrelevant); overlapping
  ranges are merged in the output (`--typescript var-decl --typescript const -j` on
  `const s = "a";` → single range `0-14`).
- The regex positional scope always intersects, and intersection requires **full
  containment**: a regex match only partially overlapping a language-scope range is
  discarded entirely. `--typescript strings 'a";'` on `const s = "a";` → nothing
  (`No input was in scope`, exit 1 in search mode); `--typescript strings -d 'c";'` on
  `const s = "abc";` → output unchanged (exit 0). `--typescript strings 'a'` → `11-12`;
  `-d 'b'` → `const s = "ac";`.
- Deletion replaces scoped bytes with nothing; line structure (newline bytes) is kept, so
  deleted multi-line nodes leave empty lines behind. E.g. deleting `class` from
  `let a = 1;\nclass K {\n  m() {}\n}\nlet b = 2;\n` yields `let a = 1;\n\n\n\nlet b = 2;\n`.

---

## 4. TypeScript prepared queries — exact scope semantics

Ranges below verified on representative inputs; "whole node" means the tree-sitter node
span including its keywords but NOT any leading `export `/`export default `/`declare `
prefix and (for methods) NOT decorators.

Reference input fragment used for several entries (line numbers refer to this block):

```ts
1  // leading comment
2  /* block
3     comment */
4  import { foo } from "mod1";
5  import * as ns from 'mod2';
6  import def from `mod3`;
7  const STR = "double";
8  const TPL = `template ${STR} end`;
9  let x = 1, y = 2;
10 var v = 3;
```

### comments
Every `comment` node, full text including the comment markers. `//`, `///`, `//!`, and
`/* ... */` all match. Multi-line block comments span all their lines.
Lines 1–3: `1:0-18`, `2:0-8`, `3:0-13`.
Comments inside strings are not comments; string-like text inside comments is not strings.

### strings
String **content only**, excluding delimiters, and **fragmented** around escape sequences
and template interpolations:
- `"double"` on line 7 → `13-19` (`double`, no quotes).
- `'...'` and template `` `...` `` behave the same (content only).
- Template interpolations `${...}` are excluded; each literal fragment is a separate
  range: line 8 → `13-22;28-32` (`` `template ${STR} end` `` → `template ` and ` end`;
  backticks excluded). Nested templates inside interpolations contribute their own
  fragment ranges (`` `multi\nline ${a + `nested ${b}`} tpl`; `` gives line1 `11-16`,
  line2 `0-5;12-19;25-29`).
- Escape sequences split the content: `"esc \" quote"` → ranges for `esc ` and ` quote`
  (`11-15;17-23`); the `\"` bytes are NOT in scope.
- Applies anywhere a string literal appears: `require("x")`, dynamic `import("x")`,
  `export { x } from "x"` module specifiers all match `strings`.

### imports
Module specifier **content** (no quotes) of `import` statements only:
- `import { foo } from "mod1";` → `21-25` (`mod1`).
- Covers `import ... from '...'`, `import "side-effect";`, and `import type { T } from "..."`.
- Does NOT cover: template-literal specifiers (`` import def from `mod3`; ``),
  `export ... from "..."` re-exports, `require("...")`, dynamic `import("...")`.

### function
Whole `function` **declarations** including the `async` keyword, excluding any
`export [default]` prefix (range starts at `async`/`function`).
`export default function main() {}` → `15-33`.
- NOT matched: arrow functions (`const f = async () => {}`), function expressions
  (`const f = function() {}`), generator declarations (`function* g() {}`,
  `async function* g() {}`), ambient declarations (`declare function f(): void;`).

### async-function / sync-function
Partition of `function`: `async function ...` declarations vs non-async `function ...`
declarations. Same exclusions as `function` (generators matched by NEITHER).

### method
Whole method definitions (`method_definition` nodes) anywhere — class bodies AND object
literals — including modifiers (`public`, `static`, `private async`, `get`/`set`,
`async *gen`) starting at the first modifier, but EXCLUDING decorators on the method.
Object-literal methods match: `{ methodInObj() { return 1; }, }` → range covers
`methodInObj() { return 1; }` (trailing comma excluded).

### constructor
Method definitions named `constructor`, whole node. Matches even in object literals
(`{ constructor() {} }`). Also included in `method` results.

### class
Whole class declarations **including decorators** (a `@dec()` line above the class is part
of the range) but excluding `export [default]` prefix.
- `abstract class` declarations are NOT matched (different node type).
- Class expressions not tested exhaustively; declarations only observed.

### enum
Whole enum declarations, excluding `export`/`declare` prefixes, but a leading `const`
modifier IS included: `const enum Fast { X }` → `0-21` (whole line);
`declare enum Ambient { Y }` → `8-26` (from `enum`).

### interface
Whole interface declarations, excluding `export` prefix.

### try-catch
Whole `try` statements including `catch` and `finally` clauses (any combination:
try/catch, try/finally, try/catch/finally).

### var-decl
Individual `variable_declarator` nodes (name through initializer), excluding the
`let`/`const`/`var` keyword and the trailing `;` or `,`:
- `const STR = "double";` → `6-20` (`STR = "double"`).
- `let x = 1, y = 2;` → `4-9;11-16` (two declarators).
- Destructuring works: `const {a, b} = obj;` → `6-18`; `const [p, q] = arr2;` → `6-19`.
- C-style `for` initializers match: `for (let i = 0; ...)` → `9-14` (`i = 0`).
- `for (const k of keys)` / `for (... in ...)` declarators do NOT match (different node).

### let / const / var
Whole declaration **statements** including the keyword and trailing `;`, excluding
`export ` prefix:
- `let x = 1, y = 2;` → `0-17` (whole line).
- `  export const inner = 1;` → const gives `9-25` (`const inner = 1;`).
- `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {}` → let gives `5-15` (`let i = 0;`).
- `for (const k of keys)` does NOT match `const`.
- `const enum E {}` does NOT match `const`.

### type-params
Whole type-parameter lists including angle brackets, on any construct (functions,
classes, interfaces, type aliases): `function sfn<T>` → `12-15` (`<T>`);
`interface Gen<T extends object>` → `13-31`; `type Pair<A, B> = ...` → `9-15`.

### type-alias
Whole `type X = ...;` declarations including `;`, excluding `export` prefix.

### namespace
Whole `namespace` blocks, excluding `export` prefix. Nested namespaces: the outer match
subsumes the inner (ranges merge in output).

### export
Whole export statements starting at the `export` keyword:
- `export { foo };`, `export default function main() {}` (whole line, `0-33`),
  `export class/interface/enum/type/namespace/const ...` (whole declaration),
  `export * from "mod-a";`, `export * as ns from "mod-b";`, `export { a as b };`.
- Inside a namespace, `  export const inner = 1;` → `2-25`.

---

## 5. C prepared queries — exact scope semantics

Reference input fragment:

```c
1  // leading comment
2  /* block
3     comment */
4  #include <stdio.h>
5  #include "local.h"
6  typedef unsigned int uint32;
7  enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };
8  struct Point {
9    int x;
10 };
11 union Value { int i; float f; };
12 int global = 42;
13 static const char *name = "hi";
14 int add(int a, int b);
15 static void helper(void) {
16   printf("in helper %d\n", global);
17 }
18 int add(int a, int b) {
19   int sum = a + b;
20   return sum;
21 }
```

### comments
All `comment` nodes incl. markers (`//` and `/* */`), like TypeScript.

### strings
**Whole string literals INCLUDING the double quotes**, and NOT fragmented by escapes:
`"hi"` → `26-30` on line 13 (quotes included); `"in helper %d\n"` → one range covering
all of it. Also matches the path of `#include` directives: `<stdio.h>` → `9-18`
(brackets included), `"local.h"` → `9-18` (quotes included).
- Character literals (`'a'`, `'\n'`) do NOT match.

### includes
Whole `#include` directive lines: `#include <stdio.h>` → `0-18`; both `<>` and `""` forms.

### type-def
Whole `typedef` declarations including the trailing `;`:
`typedef unsigned int uint32;` → `0-28`; also `typedef struct { int a; } Anon;`,
`typedef enum {...} E;`, `typedef union {...} U;` (entire statement).

### enum / struct / union
The specifier node (`enum_specifier` / `struct_specifier` / `union_specifier`) — matches
both definitions AND usages, and NEVER includes a trailing `;`:
- `enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };` → `0-29` (up to and including `}`).
- `enum Color c;` → `0-10` (`enum Color`).
- `struct Point { ... };` → lines 8–10, last line range `0-1` (`}` only; the `;` stays
  out of scope — deleting the struct leaves a lone `;` behind).
- `struct Point p;` → `0-12` (`struct Point`). `union Value u;` → `0-11`.
- Anonymous specifiers inside typedefs match: `typedef struct { int a; } Anon;` → `8-25`.

### variable
Whole `declaration` nodes (incl. `;`) that are not function definitions — at file scope,
block scope, and `for` initializers:
- `int global = 42;` → `0-16`; `static const char *name = "hi";` → `0-31`;
  `int arr[5] = {1, 2};` → `0-20`; `int *ptr;`; `struct Point p;`; `enum Color c = RED;`;
  `char s[] = "arr";`; `int (*fp)(int);` all match in full.
- Function **prototypes** match too: `int add(int a, int b);` → `0-22`.
- `for (int i = 0; ...)` → `7-17` (`int i = 0;`).
- Function parameters do NOT match.

### declaration
Byte-identical results to `variable` (same underlying `declaration` node set).

### function
"All function usages": `function_declarator` (name + parameter list) at declaration and
definition sites, plus whole `call_expression`s at call sites:
- `int add(int a, int b);` → `4-21` (`add(int a, int b)`).
- `static void helper(void) {` → `12-24` (`helper(void)`).
- `printf("in helper %d\n", global);` → `2-34` (whole call, no `;`).
- `count += add(i, 1);` → `13-22` (`add(i, 1)`).
- Function pointer declarators (`int (*fp)(int);`) do NOT match `function`.

### function-def
Whole function definitions including storage-class/specifiers and body:
`static void helper(void) {` starts at column 0 and spans through the closing `}` line.

### function-decl
All `function_declarator` nodes — both in prototypes AND in definitions:
`int add(int a, int b);` → `4-21`; `static void helper(void) {` → `12-24`;
`int add(int a, int b) {` → `4-21`; `int main(void) {` → `4-14`.
Also function-pointer declarators: `int (*fp)(int);` → `4-14` (`(*fp)(int)`).

### switch / if / for / while / do
Whole statement nodes including bodies, starting at the keyword:
- `if` covers the entire `if / else if / else` chain as one scope (with or without braces).
- `do` includes the trailing `while (...);`.
- Braceless bodies work for `if`/`for`/`while`/`do` (e.g. `while (1) g();` → `2-16`).
- QUIRK: a `switch` whose body is not a compound statement (`switch (1) case 1: break;`)
  is NOT matched (observed `No input was in scope`); with `{ ... }` it matches normally.

### identifier
All `identifier` nodes (not `type_identifier`, not `field_identifier`):
- `enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };` → `13-16;18-23` (`RED`, `GREEN`; `Color` is a
  type_identifier and is NOT matched).
- `#define MAX 10` → `8-11` (`MAX` matches).
- Declarator names, call targets, variable references match; struct/union/enum type
  names (`Point`, `Color` in `enum Color c` — wait: `enum Color c = RED;` gives
  `11-12;15-18`, i.e. `c` and `RED`; `Color` excluded), member/field names
  (`p.x`, `int x;` inside struct bodies) do NOT match.

### call-expression
Whole `call_expression` nodes: exactly the call-site subset of `function`
(`printf(...)`, `add(i, 1)`, `helper()`), without trailing `;`.

---

## 6. Input/encoding edge cases

- **Empty stdin** (0 bytes): search mode → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit 1; action mode → empty stdout, exit 0.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved; search output's last line also has no trailing
  newline. Exit 0.
- **Unicode/emoji**: fully supported; reported columns are byte offsets (UTF-8), so
  multibyte content shifts end columns. E.g. TS string `"héllo 😀"` → `11-22`;
  C identifier `café` in `int café = 1;` → `4-9`.
- **Invalid UTF-8** anywhere on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, no output (even with no language scope / plain actions).
- **CRLF**: lines split on `\n`; `\r` remains part of the printed line content
  (`// comment^M`) but never part of a scope range (`comments` on `// comment\r\n` →
  `0-10`). Deletion preserves CRLF untouched outside scopes.
- **Syntax errors**: silently tolerated (tree-sitter error recovery). No warning, exit
  follows normal rules. Whatever still parses is scoped: in
  `const x = ;\nfunction broken( {\n  "str";\n`, `--typescript strings` finds `"str"`
  content at `3:3-6`; in `int main( {\n  "str";;;\n  int = 5;\n`, `--c strings` finds
  `"str"` at `2:2-7`. Constructs that no longer parse simply don't match
  (`--c function` on the broken file → `No input was in scope`, exit 1).
- **Wrong language for the content**: no detection/validation; the chosen grammar just
  parses the text. C source `int x = "hi";` under `--typescript strings` → `9-11`
  (TS-style content-only range!); TS comment `// c` under `--c comments` → matches.

Done. Spec written to `/workspace/probes/ts-c-scopes - prepared queries for --typescript AND --c, exact scoped ranges, syntax-error and invalid-query handling.md` (the requested filename exceeded the 255-byte filesystem limit, so it was shortened). Key findings:

- **Search output format**: `(stdin):LINE:START-END[;...]:<full line>` — 1-based lines, **0-based byte offsets** (end-exclusive), ranges merge when overlapping. On a TTY the ranges and filename prefix disappear entirely; no ANSI colors anywhere, even on a TTY.
- **TS vs C `strings` differ fundamentally**: TS scopes string *content only* (quotes excluded, fragmented around escapes `\"` and `${...}` interpolations), while C scopes the *whole literal including quotes* (escapes included) plus `#include` paths; C char literals `'a'` never match.
- **Exclusions are sharp**: TS `function` skips arrow functions, function expressions, generators, and `declare function`; `abstract class` never matches `class`; C `struct`/`enum`/`union` match specifiers including usages (`struct P p;`) but exclude the trailing `;`; a braceless `switch (x) case 1: break;` is silently not matched.
- **Intersection is sequential narrowing, order matters**: `--typescript const --typescript var-decl` works but reversed yields nothing; `strings ∩ strings` fails for TS (fragments don't reparse) yet works for C (quotes preserved). Regex intersections require full containment — partial overlaps are discarded entirely.
- **Error taxonomy**: zero matches in *search mode* → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit 1, but in *action mode* no-match is silently exit 0; invalid prepared values → clap error listing all possible values, exit 2; invalid custom queries → verbatim tree-sitter `Query error at row:col` messages, exit 1; a capture-less valid query compiles but scopes nothing.
- **Quirks**: the two-language error hardcodes `Usage: srgn` while other errors use argv0; syntax-broken input is silently tolerated with partial scoping; invalid UTF-8 aborts with exit 1; `--count` doesn't exist despite the README; env vars `TYPESCRIPT`/`C` and alias `--ts` work.
